note: Per-round ledger of this target's review history. The commit/merge gate keys freshness on the sibling record (<key>.json) — a fresh review of the exact reviewed bytes — but --record now refuses to file a record unless this ledger's last round reviewed those same bytes, so a record can never be filed for content the ledger never saw. This file is the history the record itself cannot carry: what each round found, what was fixed, what was refuted by execution. Rounds are appended in order; a header key already present is never rewritten or dropped by a later append.

findings_fixed: Round 1 (on 680d4ea) found three test defects, all fixed in fbfc01b: a check named 'only the exact =1 spelling is tolerated' was false (comparison is on dequoted text, so the quoted value spellings are admitted) and now tests =0/=11/=1x/empty denied plus the three quoted spellings admitted and a quoted assignment NAME denied; a vacuous compose check that short-circuited at has_skip_prefix before the grammar was renamed to say what it pins and backed with a positive end-to-end case reaching exit 0 through parse_invocation; the environment route for KARTA_SKIP_GATE was untested and is now pinned as non-bypassing. Docstring and ALLOWED_PREFIXES comment corrected: not a generic KARTA_ allowlist, membership is permission to appear and never approval.
findings_refuted_or_deferred: Round 1: Copilot rated the interpolated denial message a HIGH information leak — refuted, the three variable names are documented in AGENTS.md, in docs/how-to/roundtable.md, and printed by the sibling gate's own denial; the hook exists to tell a human how to proceed. Kimi posited a mirror deadlock where the sibling gate denies KARTA_SKIP_ROUNDTABLE=1 — verified false, it has no prefix grammar and denies no prefixes.
rounds.notes: Round 2 reviewed the final branch state (fbfc01b) and is unanimous to land across six providers: Ship it (kimi), I would approve this landing (glm), sound (deepseek/minimax/qwen), safe to land (copilot). No bypass found in either round. Known-open and deliberately NOT fixed: the skip hatch returns from decide() before the safety grammar, so a relocating GIT_INDEX_FILE prefix rides along with the hatch. Pre-existing, pinned by a test named 'the skip hatch is evaluated before every other rule', and judged defensible by every panelist that addressed it. Two low nits accepted but deferred to keep the record byte-exact to what was reviewed: module docstring does not mention the tolerated prefix, and the 'not denied as an illegal prefix' check should also assert code == 2. Antigravity produced no output (headless permission denial) and Codex errored on a stale model id; 6 of 8 panelists returned verdicts.
